w10_P4_002308: A pumping station's plant figure is a hall force in kilonewtons plus 11 kN for the base slab. The hall force covers 12 identical banks, and each bank has 8 identical rams pushing together. One ram drives a mass of 46 kg. That mass's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 12 times the value, plus 32, equals exactly 0. The station's outfall pipe is 300 m long. What is the plant figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002309: A rail depot's shed figure is 11 times the force taken by a single bay, expressed in kilonewtons. A bay drives a wagon of mass 173 kg. The wagon's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is a meter total minus 5. That total is what the bay's meter accumulates between the 1st and the 4th second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 2 times t squared plus 3 times t. The depot's inspection pit is 30 m long. What is the shed figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002310: A dockside conveyor's site figure is twice a bay total, because two identical bays run at the same time. A bay total is 5 times a single sack's booked energy, expressed in kilojoules. A sack's booked energy is its kinetic energy less 7 J absorbed by the chute liner. The sack has a mass of 56000 g, and its speed, in metres per second, equals the total the chute meter accumulates between the 2nd and the 3rd second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 5 times t squared plus 1 times t. What is the site figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_002315: A quarry's shift figure is 11 times a net cycle figure, expressed in kilojoules. A net cycle figure is the combined energy of 6 identical skips, less 21 J absorbed by the tipping latch. A skip has a mass of 46000 g. Its speed, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 13 times the value, plus 42, equals exactly 0. What is the quarry's shift figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_002316: A hydro test flume meters its gate through a surge, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 3 times t squared plus 3 times t. The float's speed, in metres per second, is the total accumulated between the 1st and the 3rd second, plus 20. The float has a mass of 55 kg. The run sheet takes the float's kinetic energy and adds 19 J drawn by the gate motor. Four identical flumes run together, and the site log then subtracts 19 J credited back by the recovery turbine. What does the site log record, in J?
w10_P4_002320: A workshop's balance sheet is a driving force in kilonewtons, less 12 kN for the granite base and then a further 10 kN for the anti-vibration mounts. The driven slide has a mass of 37 kg, and the workshop's extractor draws 250 W. The slide's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 13 times the value, plus 40, equals exactly 0. What does the balance sheet give, in kN?
w10_P4_002321: A wave-tank rig meters its paddle through a stroke, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 5 times t squared plus 6 times t. The float's speed, in metres per second, equals the total accumulated between the 0th and the 1st second. The float has a mass of 18000 g, and the rig's control lamp draws 45 W. The run sheet takes the float's kinetic energy and subtracts 11 J drawn by the paddle motor, and the rig runs a mirrored second tank, doubling the figure. What does the run sheet give, in kJ?
w10_P4_002328: A brick works drives a ram carrying a mass of 98 kg. The ram's position along its guide, in metres, is 2 times the cube of the elapsed seconds plus 0 times the square of the elapsed seconds, and the works takes how fast it is moving at the instant 1 second in as the acceleration in metres per second squared. Seven identical rams work each press, and the press log then adds 14 N for the ejector spring. The works operates 6 identical presses. What total force do the works' presses supply, in N?
w10_P4_002338: A packing line drives a pallet of mass 124000 g. The pallet's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is found by taking the number of different groups of 3 that can be chosen from the line's 6 pick points, subtracting 7, and then adding 11. Eight identical pallets run at once, and the line's log then adds 7 N for the load-cell offset. The line's shrink oven is rated at 15 kW. What does the line's log record, in N?
w10_P4_002346: A dry dock's gate rig drives a caisson of mass 192 kg on its scale model. The caisson's acceleration, in metres per second squared, equals the total the model's meter accumulates between the 0th and the 3rd second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 2 times t squared plus 3 times t. The rig's log subtracts 12 N for the seal drag. Expressed in kilonewtons, the yard sheet then adds 10 kN for the sill anchors. The yard operates 5 identical gates, and its report gives 5 times the single-gate figure. What does the report give, in kN?
w10_P4_002348: A tunnelling contractor's site figure is 7 times a machine's total, expressed in kilonewtons. A machine's total is the combined push of its 9 identical rams, plus 2 N for the load-pin offset. One ram drives a mass of 23 kg at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, equal to the total its meter accumulates between the 1st and the 3rd second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 4 times t squared plus 1 times t. The site's ventilation duct is 600 m long. What is the contractor's site figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002350: A tannery receives 191 hides of one grade and 82 of another, and it stacks them into identical bundles using the largest bundle size that divides both counts exactly. A test carriage of mass 99000 g is then driven at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, equal to that bundle size plus 6. The works' log takes the driving force and adds 5 N for the rail drag. It then adds a further 23 N for the guide brushes. What does the log record, in N?
w10_P4_002364: A freight operator's annual figure is 12 times its monthly figure, and the monthly figure is 12 times a week's total in kilojoules. A week's total covers 9 identical wagon runs, so it is 9 times the energy of one wagon. A wagon has a mass of 56000 g on the scale model used for the estimate. Its speed, in metres per second, equals the total the model's meter accumulates between the 3rd and the 4th second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 4 times t squared plus 1 times t. What is the operator's annual figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_002369: A drop-test facility's site figure is 5 times a rig total, and a rig total is a bay's energy plus 4 J for the release magnet. A bay's energy covers 7 identical drops, so it is 7 times the energy of one carrier. A carrier has a mass of 49 kg. Its release speed, in metres per second, is read from a calibration chart on which a plotted quantity equals 4 times the cube of the dial setting plus 6 times the square of the dial setting; the speed is the second-order rate of change of that plotted quantity with respect to the dial setting, evaluated at a dial setting of 2. What is the facility's site figure, in J?
w10_P4_002377: A gantry test hall drives a block of mass 163 kg. The block's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 4 times the sum of the two drive-dial readings, which are 5 and 11. The hall's log subtracts 26 N for the guide-shoe friction. Expressed in kilonewtons, the site sheet then subtracts 29 kN allowed for the frame's own restraint. The hall's roof beam spans 22 m. Five identical halls run the same test, and the report gives 5 times the single-hall figure. What does the report give, in kN?
w10_P4_002384: A bridge-launch contractor's site figure is a nose force in kilonewtons plus 22 kN for the launch bearings. The nose force is 5 times the force driving a single segment, since five identical segments are pushed together. A segment has a mass of 188 kg on the scale rig, and the rig's floodlight draws 300 W. A segment's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the number of different pairs that can be chosen from the rig's 10 tie points, taking 2 at a time. What is the contractor's site figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002393: A lab's daily balance is an energy figure in kilojoules, less 23 kJ drawn by the chiller. That figure is the cart's kinetic energy plus 6 J for the release catch and then a further 30 J for the timer. The cart has a mass of 12 kg, and the lab's bench lamp draws 40 W. The cart's speed, in metres per second, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 7 times the value, plus 12, equals exactly 0. What is the lab's daily balance, in kJ?
w10_P4_002394: A crane hire firm's fleet figure is 9 times a site's total, expressed in kilonewtons. A site's total is the frame force plus 13 kN for the outrigger pads. A frame carries 8 identical hoists pulling together, and one hoist drives a load of mass 46000 g. That load's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the number of different pairs that can be chosen from the frame's 12 anchor eyes, taking 2 at a time. The firm's yard fence runs 90 m. What is the firm's fleet figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002395: A toboggan centre's day figure is 10 times a single run's energy, expressed in kilojoules. A rider and sled together have a mass of 41000 g. Their speed, in metres per second, is built up as follows: twice the sum of the two gradient-dial readings, which are 6 and 8, then 19 subtracted, and the result multiplied by 5. What is the centre's day figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_002396: A gym's test rig drops a weight of mass 27000 g onto a padded stop. The weight's impact speed, in metres per second, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 12 times the value, plus 35, equals exactly 0. The rig's sheet takes the weight's kinetic energy, adds 24 J drawn by the release magnet, and then adds a further 3 J for the timer. Two identical rigs run side by side, and the gym holds 11 identical sessions in a week. How much energy does a week account for, in J?
w10_P4_002399: A funicular's weekly figure is 7 times a day's booked energy, expressed in kilojoules. A day's booked energy is the car's kinetic energy plus 23 kJ drawn by the haulage house. The car has a mass of 47000 g on the scale model used for the estimate. Its speed, in metres per second, is 6 times the largest whole number that divides both 101 and 174 exactly. What is the funicular's weekly figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_002401: A laboratory rig's report is a frame balance with 23 kN then added for the tie-down bolts. The frame balance is the combined force of 7 identical actuators, expressed in kilonewtons, less 22 kN allowed for the granite base. One actuator drives a mass of 19 kg, and the rig's controller draws 90 W. That mass's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 5 times the value, plus 6, equals exactly 0. What does the rig's report give, in kN?
w10_P4_002402: A shipfitting bay's hall figure is 12 times a single jig's corrected force. A jig's corrected force is the force on its frame, plus 27 N for the roller drag and then a further 22 N for the clamp preload. The frame has a mass of 33 kg. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the number of different groups of 3 that can be chosen from the jig's 8 pick-up lugs. What is the bay's hall figure, in N?
w10_P4_002406: A cider works' plant figure is 8 times a line total, and a line total is 6 times a single crate's booked energy. A crate's booked energy is its kinetic energy plus 16 J drawn by the indexing motor. The crate has a mass of 13 kg, and its speed, in metres per second, is 3 times a base number. That base number is the largest whole number that divides both 286 and 400 exactly. What is the works' plant figure, in J?
w10_P4_002408: A bakery's floor figure is the force taken by its 12 identical frames, expressed in kilonewtons. Each frame carries 7 identical pushers working together. One pusher drives a tray of mass 20000 g. That tray's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 124 and 357 exactly. What is the bakery's floor figure, in kN?
